location: Section 3.11 step 5 (PowerShell command `Get-FileHash ... | Format-Table -AutoSize Hash, Path`)
problem: In a normal PowerShell window (120 columns), Format-Table cuts off the Path column before the file name. Each row needs about 156 characters even from C:\work, so the student cannot tell which hash belongs to which figure.
evidence: `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 artifacts/dirac16complex/kohn-sham/figures/*.png | Format-Table -AutoSize Hash, Path | Out-String -Width 120` printed rows like `5C5F...F6B C:\Users\nsh\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--Developer-gi...`. With the recommended C:\work clone, a row is 65 + 64 + name = up to 156 characters, which is more than 120.
fix: Use a command that prints the file name, in lower case to match Section 2.4. For example: `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 artifacts/dirac16complex/kohn-sham/figures/*.png | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Hash.ToLower())  $(Split-Path -Leaf $_.Path)" }`. Use the same pattern in step 6.

problem: The macOS commands were never run, and the file does not say so. Section 6.1 lists only Windows and Linux, but Section 3 presents the macOS commands and results as equivalent.
